headline: GOLD GIVES BACK $73 FROM ELECTION HIGH — Post-Election Profit-Taking Pulls Spot to $4,063; Dollar Steadies
snippet: Spot gold retreated from its overnight election-surge high of $4,136.60 — the highest in two weeks — to $4,063.15 by mid-morning on November 6 as the U.S. dollar found footing after its post-midterm drop. The $73 intraday pullback represents roughly 1.8% profit-taking from the peak, though gold remains nearly $200 above October's intraday low of $3,875 as the broader bull structure stays intact.

headline: YANGSHAN COPPER PREMIUM HITS $210/t — MATCHING 2013 RECORD as China Physical Demand Surges Despite LME Paper Rout
snippet: China's Yangshan copper import premium surged to $210 per tonne on November 5, matching a record last seen in 2013, as physical demand for copper from Chinese buyers intensified even as LME three-month copper slid to multi-month lows near $13,768 on post-election macro concerns. The premium — a leading indicator of Chinese appetite for imported copper — signals that the paper selloff has disconnected sharply from actual end-user demand on the ground.

headline: IVANHOE SLASHES KAMOA-KAKULA AGAIN — 2027 Output CUT 19% to 300-350kt; Stock Hits 4-YEAR LOW
snippet: Ivanhoe Mines issued a third production downgrade for Kamoa-Kakula alongside Q3 results on November 3-4, cutting its 2027 guidance by 19% to 300,000–350,000 tonnes — down from a previous 380,000–420,000 tonne target — as flood-related recovery work takes longer than expected at the DRC's flagship copper complex. Full-year 2026 output is now expected at approximately 290,000 tonnes, and the stock touched a four-year low as analysts flagged the path back to 500,000+ tonnes as 'longer, more capital intensive, and more dependent on future execution.'

headline: SURGE COPPER WRAPS BERG 2026 CAMPAIGN — 6,334m Drilled Across 31 Holes in BC Toodoggone; Assay Package Pending
snippet: Surge Copper (TSXV: SURG) completed its 2026 drill program at the Berg copper-molybdenum project in British Columbia's Toodoggone district, finishing 6,334.5 metres across 31 holes. All assays from the program are now being processed and results will be released as they are received; Berg is a large porphyry system that management believes is significantly under-drilled relative to the scale of the mineralized footprint.

headline: MALAWI SENDS FIRST URANIUM — LOTUS RESOURCES 145,000 LBS U3O8 Departs Kayelekera for European Converter
snippet: Lotus Resources (ASX: LOT) confirmed on November 2 that the inaugural shipment of uranium ore concentrate — four containers holding approximately 145,000 pounds of U3O8 — departed the Kayelekera mine in Malawi for Namibia's Walvis Bay port, bound for the Orano CE conversion facility in France. The milestone marks the first uranium export from Malawi's newly restarted mine and adds a new African supplier to the tight uranium market as spot prices approach US$92 per pound.

headline: KINROSS Q3 RESULTS FRIDAY — AISC $1,850-1,900/oz Guidance Intact; RECORD Free Cash Flow Expected at $4,100 Gold
snippet: Kinross Gold reports Q3 2026 results on November 7, with management guidance calling for all-in sustaining costs of approximately $1,850–$1,900 per gold-equivalent ounce — a range set when gold was well below current spot levels of $4,100+. Analysts widely expect Kinross to report record free cash flow for the quarter, and the stock was flagged as a top watch ahead of earnings given its leverage to the gold price surge following the Democratic midterm sweep.

headline: BUY AGNICO EAGLE ON THE DIP — CNBC's Seymour: AEM a 'Cash Machine' Down 30% From 52-Week High
snippet: CNBC Fast Money trader Tim Seymour made the bull case for Agnico Eagle (TSX: AEM) on November 3, arguing the gold miner is a 'cash machine' that remains meaningfully undervalued at roughly 30% below its 52-week high. Seymour highlighted that Agnico's management expects to return more than half of its 2026 free cash flow through dividends and buybacks, and that its cost structure and mine quality justify a re-rating as gold consolidates above $4,000.

headline: TED OAKLEY: TRIM GOLD MINERS BEFORE 2027 — Market Strategist Cautious at CAPE 40; 'Won't Add at $4,100'
snippet: Veteran market strategist Ted Oakley says he is cautious on gold miners heading into 2027 — holding existing positions but refusing to add at current levels as the S&P 500 Shiller CAPE ratio approaches 40.1, credit markets flash early-warning signals, and the gold sector has attracted crowded momentum positioning following the post-election surge to $4,100+. Oakley's view is a minority one but represents the main bear case that retail investors should stress-test before adding gold miner exposure.

headline: FIVE CANADIAN GOLD JUNIORS BELOW THE RADAR — Report Flags Undervalued TSXV Names as Retail Attention Locks on Majors
snippet: A fresh Canadian Mining Report analysis identifies five TSX Venture-listed gold junior miners it considers undervalued at current gold prices above $4,100, arguing that retail investor and media attention is disproportionately concentrated on large producers like Newmont and Barrick while junior-tier explorers with strong balance sheets and near-term catalysts remain trading well below the implied value at spot. The report does not constitute investment advice but provides a starting screen for self-directed investors.

headline: AUSTRALIA PROPOSES STRATEGIC REE RESERVE — Canberra Eyes Critical Minerals Stockpile as China Nov. 10 Deadline Nears
snippet: Canberra has outlined a proposed Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve focused on rare earth elements, joining Germany's Chancellor Merz in calling for Western nations to build physical stockpiles ahead of China's expanded rare earth export control pause expiring November 10. Australia, as home to significant REE deposits and a key partner in the AUKUS framework, is positioning the reserve as both a supply security measure and an economic lever as global demand for dysprosium, terbium, and NdPr accelerates.
